title: Rondo 4v1
instructions: Set up a 10x10 yard square with cones.
Four players stand on the outside, one defender in the middle.
Outside players must pass the ball around, keeping possession.
The defender tries to intercept or win the ball.
If the defender wins the ball, the player who made the bad pass becomes the defender.
Two-touch maximum for outside players.
coachingPoints: Open body shape to see all passing options.
Play the way you face when under pressure.
Quick ball movement — don't hold onto the ball.
Communicate with teammates.
variations: One-touch only for advanced players.
Increase to 5v2 for more challenge.
Expand or shrink the grid to adjust difficulty.

title: Wall Pass & Shoot
instructions: Player A starts with the ball 30 yards from goal.
Player B stands 10 yards ahead as the wall passer.
Player A passes to Player B and makes a run into the box.
Player B lays the ball off first-time into Player A's path.
Player A shoots first-time or with one touch.
Rotate roles after each attempt.
coachingPoints: Weight of the pass must be firm enough to play one-touch.
Timing of the run — don't go too early.
Shoot across the goalkeeper to the far post.
Follow up for rebounds.
variations: Add a passive defender to create pressure.
Alternate sides (left and right).
Require weak-foot finish.

title: 1v1 Dribble Gates
instructions: Set up 4 small gates (2 yards wide) in a 20x20 yard area.
Players pair up — one attacker, one defender.
Attacker scores a point by dribbling through any gate.
Defender tries to win the ball or force the attacker away from gates.
Play for 1 minute, then switch roles.
Keep score — most points wins.
coachingPoints: Keep the ball close and use changes of direction.
Use body feints to unbalance the defender.
Scan for open gates before committing.
Accelerate through the gate once you've beaten the defender.
variations: Add more gates for beginners.
Reduce the area for more intensity.
Allow defender to score by dribbling through gates if they win the ball.

title: Pressing Triggers 6v4
instructions: Mark out a 40x30 yard zone split into two halves.
6 attacking players (blue) try to keep possession across both halves.
4 defenders (red) press and try to win the ball.
Pressing trigger: when a back-pass is made, defenders sprint to close down.
If defenders win the ball, they try to score through mini goals.
Play for 3 minutes, then rotate defenders.
coachingPoints: Identify the pressing trigger — backward or sideways pass.
Press as a unit, not individually.
Cover shadow: cut off the next passing lane while pressing the ball.
Recover quickly if the press is broken.
variations: Change to 6v3 for easier pressing.
Add a neutral player who plays for the team in possession.
Require 8 passes for a point to increase pressing urgency.

title: Shuttle Runs with Ball
instructions: Set up cones at 5, 10, 15, and 20 yards from the start line.
Players dribble to the 5-yard cone, turn, and dribble back.
Then dribble to 10-yard cone and back, 15 and back, 20 and back.
Rest for 30 seconds.
Repeat for 4 sets.
coachingPoints: Keep the ball under close control during turns.
Use the sole of the foot to stop and turn quickly.
Maintain a high tempo throughout each set.
Focus on clean turns, not just speed.
variations: Without the ball for pure fitness.
Add a pass to a partner at each cone.
Time each set and try to beat your personal best.

title: Triangular Passing Pattern
instructions: Set up three cones in a triangle, 15 yards apart.
Two players at each cone.
Player A passes to Player B, then follows the pass to B's cone.
Player B receives, opens up, and passes to Player C, then follows.
Pattern continues — always follow your pass.
Increase speed gradually.
coachingPoints: Receive on the back foot to open your body.
Pass with pace — firm, driven passes along the ground.
Check your shoulder before receiving.
Sprint to the next cone after passing.
variations: Add a one-two before passing to the next station.
Play one-touch only.
Add a fourth cone to create a diamond pattern.

title: Finishing from Crosses
instructions: Set up with a full-size goal and a goalkeeper.
Wide player starts on the right wing with a supply of balls.
Two attackers start at the edge of the box.
Wide player dribbles to the byline and crosses.
Attackers make near-post and far-post runs to finish.
Add a defender after 5 minutes to create realistic pressure.
coachingPoints: Stagger runs — near post first, far post second.
Attack the ball aggressively — don't wait for it.
Aim for the target on first contact.
Far-post runner should arrive slightly later.
variations: Cross from the left side.
Add cutback crosses from the byline.
Include a midfielder arriving late for knock-downs.

title: Skill Dribble Course
instructions: Set up 8 cones in a zigzag pattern, 3 yards apart.
Dribble through all cones using the inside and outside of the foot.
At the last cone, turn and dribble back.
Focus on technique first, then increase speed.
Complete 5 full runs.
coachingPoints: Keep the ball close — small touches.
Use both feet throughout the course.
Keep your head up as much as possible.
Bend the knees and stay low for balance.
variations: Use only the weak foot.
Add a step-over at each cone.
Race against a partner for competition.

title: Back Line Shifting
instructions: Four defenders form a back line across the pitch.
Four attackers pass the ball across the front.
Defenders must shift as a unit following the ball.
When the ball goes wide, the nearest defender presses.
Remaining defenders tuck in and cover.
Coach calls 'play' — attackers try to penetrate with a through ball.
coachingPoints: Move as a unit — stay connected.
Ball-side defender applies pressure, others provide cover.
Don't ball-watch — scan for runners.
Communicate constantly: 'shift left', 'hold', 'step up'.
variations: Add a midfielder to help the back line.
Allow attackers to overlap for realistic scenarios.
Progress to full 8v8 with build-up from the back.

title: HIIT Ball Mastery
instructions: Set up 6 stations in a circle, 5 yards apart.
Station 1: Toe taps on the ball (20 seconds on, 10 seconds rest).
Station 2: Ball rolls side-to-side (20 seconds on, 10 seconds rest).
Station 3: Around-the-world dribble (20 seconds on, 10 seconds rest).
Station 4: Quick feet shuffle with ball (20 seconds on, 10 seconds rest).
Station 5: Sprint to cone and back with ball (20 seconds on, 10 seconds rest).
Station 6: Juggling (20 seconds on, 10 seconds rest).
Complete 4 full circuits.
coachingPoints: Maximum effort during work periods.
Use rest periods to recover — don't waste them.
Focus on ball control even when tired.
Stay on the balls of your feet.
variations: Extend work periods to 30 seconds.
Reduce rest periods to 5 seconds.
Add partner challenges at each station.

title: Switch of Play Diamond
instructions: Set up a large diamond shape with cones, roughly 40 yards wide and 30 yards tall.
Place one player at each cone and two in the center.
Ball starts at the bottom of the diamond — pass to a central player.
Central player opens up and plays a long switch to the opposite wide cone.
Wide player receives, controls, and plays into the other central player.
Pattern continues: always look to switch the ball through the middle.
Rotate positions every 3 minutes.
coachingPoints: First touch should set the ball for the switch — receive across your body.
Long passes must be driven and accurate, not floated.
Central players must constantly check their shoulders.
Receiving players should show for the ball at an angle.
variations: Add two defenders in the middle to create pressure.
One-touch only in the center.
Progress to playing into a final third and finishing.

title: Give & Go Circuit
instructions: Set up 4 stations in a square, 15 yards apart, with a cone at each.
Place a mannequin or passive player 5 yards from each station.
Player passes to the wall player, sprints around the mannequin, and receives the return pass.
Carry the ball to the next station and repeat.
Complete full circuits — one clockwise, one counter-clockwise.
coachingPoints: Pass must be crisp and to feet — no bobbling passes.
Sprint immediately after playing the ball — don't admire your pass.
Receive on the move, don't stop and wait.
Use both feet — pass with the right going one way, left the other.
variations: One-touch wall passes only.
Add a time challenge — fastest circuit wins.
Include a shot on goal at the final station.

title: Volley Finishing
instructions: Goalkeeper in goal. Server stands 25 yards out to the side.
Striker starts at the penalty spot facing the server.
Server tosses or chips the ball toward the striker.
Striker must volley or half-volley first-time into the goal.
Alternate serves from left and right side.
10 attempts per player, then rotate.
coachingPoints: Watch the ball all the way onto your foot.
Lock the ankle and keep your knee over the ball.
Aim for placement over power — pick your corner.
Adjust body shape quickly based on the flight of the ball.
variations: Add a passive defender to block the shot.
Require headers from crossed serves.
Serve from further away to simulate game crosses.

title: Penalty Box Chaos
instructions: Goalkeeper in goal. 3-4 shooters line up at the edge of the box.
Coach plays balls into the box randomly — bouncing, rolling, in the air.
First player in line attacks the ball and shoots first-time.
After shooting, immediately clear the box for the next player.
Coach varies the type of delivery to simulate unpredictable game situations.
Play for 5 minutes, count goals, then rotate goalkeeper.
coachingPoints: React quickly — don't overthink, just shoot.
Use whichever foot the ball arrives on.
Keep shots low and on target — beat the keeper, don't blast over.
Be alert and ready before the ball is played.
variations: Add a defender to pressure the shooter.
Two players race for the ball — first to shoot.
Limit touches to one.

title: Cruyff Turn & Accelerate
instructions: Set up pairs of cones 10 yards apart in a line.
Dribble toward the first cone at jogging pace.
At the cone, perform a Cruyff turn — fake to kick, drag the ball behind your standing leg.
Explode with the ball toward the next cone.
Perform the Cruyff turn again and accelerate back.
Complete 8 repetitions, alternating which foot performs the turn.
coachingPoints: Sell the fake — shape your body as if you're going to pass or shoot.
Use the inside of the foot to drag the ball behind you.
Accelerate immediately after the turn — the first 3 steps are crucial.
Keep the ball close throughout the move.
variations: Add a step-over before the Cruyff turn.
Introduce a passive defender to beat with the turn.
Chain Cruyff turns with other moves (e.g., Cruyff into a chop).

title: Dribble Under Pressure 2v1
instructions: Mark a 20x15 yard channel leading to a mini goal.
Attacker starts with the ball at one end, defender starts 10 yards ahead.
A support player stands wide as a passing option but cannot score.
Attacker must dribble past the defender and score — using the support player is allowed.
If the defender wins the ball, they try to dribble out through the start line.
Play 1 minute rounds, then rotate all positions.
coachingPoints: Commit the defender before deciding to dribble or pass.
Attack the defender's front foot at pace.
Use the support player to unbalance the defender, then take them on.
Be decisive — half-hearted dribbles get tackled.
variations: Remove the support player for pure 1v1.
Add a second defender to make it 2v2.
Require a specific skill move to beat the defender.

title: Recovery Run Challenge
instructions: Set up a 30-yard channel with a goal at one end.
Attacker starts at the halfway point with the ball, facing the goal.
Defender starts 5 yards behind the attacker, facing away.
On the coach's whistle, the defender turns and sprints to recover.
Attacker tries to score before the defender can make a tackle or block.
Play 5 rounds per pair, then switch roles.
coachingPoints: Sprint at full speed to get goalside — take the shortest recovery line.
Don't dive in when you arrive — get your body between the ball and the goal.
Slow down and jockey once you're goalside.
Force the attacker wide, away from the goal center.
variations: Increase the defender's starting distance for harder recovery.
Add a second attacker for 2v1 recovery situations.
Start the defender on the ground (simulating getting up after a tackle).

title: Zonal Marking from Crosses
instructions: Full-size goal with a goalkeeper. Mark 3 zones in the box: near post, central, far post.
Assign one defender to each zone.
A wide player delivers crosses from the wing.
3 attackers make runs into the box trying to score from the cross.
Defenders must win the ball in their zone — clear it or catch it (if GK).
Play 10 crosses, count goals conceded, then rotate.
coachingPoints: Own your zone — attack the ball, don't let it come to you.
Get your body in front of the attacker before the ball arrives.
Head the ball up, away, and wide — not back toward goal.
Communicate with the goalkeeper and adjacent defenders.
variations: Switch to man-marking to compare effectiveness.
Add a second crosser for cutback deliveries.
Include a midfielder arriving late from deep.

title: Sprint Interval Ladders
instructions: Set up 5 cones in a line at 10, 20, 30, 40, and 50 yards.
Round 1: Sprint to 10-yard cone, jog back. Sprint to 20-yard cone, jog back.
Continue the ladder — sprint to each cone and jog back to the start.
After reaching the 50-yard cone, work back down: 40, 30, 20, 10.
Rest 60 seconds between full ladders.
Complete 3 full ladders.
coachingPoints: Explode out of each start — drive with the arms.
Stay on the balls of your feet — no flat-footed jogging.
Use the jog back as active recovery, don't walk.
Maintain sprint quality — don't let form break down when tired.
variations: Add a ball — dribble out, pass to a partner, sprint back.
Side shuffle or backpedal instead of sprinting.
Pair up and race to each cone.

title: Agility Box Footwork
instructions: Set up a 5x5 yard square with cones at each corner.
Start at one corner. Sprint forward to the next cone.
Shuffle sideways to the next cone.
Backpedal to the next cone.
Shuffle sideways back to the start.
Complete the box 6 times, rest 30 seconds, then repeat in the opposite direction.
3 total sets.
coachingPoints: Stay low and athletic throughout — bent knees, weight on toes.
During shuffles, don't cross your feet.
Backpedal with short, choppy steps — don't turn and run.
Touch each cone as you arrive for accountability.
variations: Add a ball — dribble while performing each movement pattern.
Coach calls out random directions for reaction training.
Increase box size to 10x10 yards for more endurance demand.

title: Overlap & Cross
instructions: Set up on one half of the pitch with a full-size goal.
Full-back starts deep with the ball. Winger starts wide and high.
Full-back passes to the winger's feet.
Winger receives and plays inside, drawing the imaginary defender.
Full-back overlaps around the winger on the outside.
Winger plays a through ball for the overlapping full-back.
Full-back crosses into the box for two strikers to finish.
coachingPoints: Timing of the overlap — don't go too early or the winger has no one to pass to.
Winger must check inside first to create the space for the overlap.
Cross should be driven into the danger zone between keeper and defenders.
Strikers: stagger near and far post runs.
variations: Add a covering defender to pressure the crosser.
Alternate between left and right side overlaps.
Double overlap — winger then midfielder overlaps the full-back.

title: Turn & Shoot
instructions: Striker starts with back to goal at the edge of the penalty area.
Server plays a firm pass into the striker's feet from 15 yards behind.
Striker receives, takes a touch to turn, and shoots on goal.
Alternate receiving on the left and right side to practice both turns.
After 5 attempts, add a passive defender behind the striker.
10 shots per player, then rotate.
coachingPoints: Check your shoulder before the ball arrives to know where the goal is.
First touch must take you toward goal — don't let it bounce off you.
Use your body to shield the ball from the defender during the turn.
Strike early — the longer you wait, the more time the keeper has to set.
variations: Active defender who can tackle.
Require a specific turn (Cruyff, drag-back, spin).
Add a one-two option with a support player.

title: La Pausa Passing Square
instructions: Set up a 25x25 yard square with cones. Place a 5x5 yard inner square in the center.
Four outside players position at the midpoints of each side. Four players work inside.
Inside players combine to play the ball from one outside player to the opposite side.
The ball must pass through the central square at least once per sequence.
Outside players are two-touch, inside players are one-touch.
After every 3 minutes, inside and outside players rotate.
coachingPoints: Inside players must constantly adjust position to offer passing angles.
Use 'La Pausa' — the brief pause before accelerating the pass to wrong-foot pressure.
Body shape open to the field, not just to the ball.
Weight of pass must be precise — firm but playable.
variations: Add two defenders inside to press.
One-touch for everyone.
Score a point only if the switch is completed in under 4 seconds.

title: Power Shot Stations
instructions: Set up three shooting stations at 20, 25, and 30 yards from goal.
Place a cone at each station. Goalkeeper in goal.
Player starts at Station 1 (20 yards) — receives a lay-off from a server and shoots first-time.
Immediately moves to Station 2 (25 yards) — drives forward with the ball and strikes.
Finally moves to Station 3 (30 yards) — hits a dead ball aiming for a specific corner.
Complete all three stations, then join the back of the line. 3 full rounds per player.
coachingPoints: Plant foot next to the ball, pointing at the target.
Strike through the center of the ball for power, slightly below center for loft.
Follow through fully — don't stab at the ball.
Keep your head steady and eyes on the ball at the moment of contact.
variations: Weak foot only at one or more stations.
Add a wall of mannequins to shoot over or around.
Require a curl shot at Station 3 instead of power.

title: Elastico & Go
instructions: Set up 5 cones in a straight line, 4 yards apart.
Dribble at moderate speed toward the first cone.
Perform an elastico (outside-inside flick with the same foot) to go around the cone.
Accelerate to the next cone and repeat.
At the last cone, perform a sharp turn and dribble back using the other foot.
Complete 6 full runs. Rest 30 seconds between each.
coachingPoints: The elastico is one fluid motion — push outside, snap inside with the same foot.
Drop the shoulder opposite to the direction you want to go to sell the fake.
Keep the ball on the ground — don't scoop it.
Explode past the cone after each elastico — the move is wasted without acceleration.
variations: Alternate between elastico and step-over at each cone.
Add a passive defender at every second cone.
Finish with a shot on goal after the final cone.

title: Counter-Press 3v3
instructions: Set up a 25x20 yard grid with a mini goal at each end.
Two teams of 3 play inside the grid.
Normal possession rules — score in the opponent's mini goal.
When a team loses the ball, they have 5 seconds to win it back (counter-press).
If they win it back within 5 seconds, a goal counts double.
If they fail to win it back, they must drop into a compact defensive shape.
coachingPoints: Immediate reaction on losing the ball — nearest player must press the ball instantly.
Other two players cut off passing lanes, don't all chase the ball.
Hunt in pairs — one presses, one covers the next pass.
Transition mindset: attack one second, defend the next.
variations: Increase to 4v4 in a bigger grid.
Add neutral wide players who play for the team in possession.
Remove the 5-second rule and just reward counter-press goals.

title: Yo-Yo Endurance Runs
instructions: Mark three lines: start, 20 yards, and a recovery zone 5 yards behind the start.
Players run 20 yards out and 20 yards back within a set time window.
After each shuttle, jog to the recovery zone and back (10 seconds active rest).
Start at a slow pace. Each level increases the required speed.
If a player fails to reach the line before the beep twice, they are eliminated.
Continue until all players are eliminated or 20 minutes is reached.
coachingPoints: Pace yourself in the early levels — don't sprint from the start.
Turn efficiently — decelerate in 2-3 steps, pivot, and drive out.
Use the recovery jog wisely — control breathing.
Mental toughness matters as much as fitness in the later levels.
variations: Add a ball — dribble the shuttle for football-specific endurance.
Team format: each player's level adds to a team total score.
Perform a skill move at each turning point.

title: Third Man Run Pattern
instructions: Set up three stations in an L-shape: Player A (deep), Player B (central), Player C (high and wide).
Player A passes to Player B. Player B sets the ball back first-time.
Player A plays a through ball into the space behind for Player C, who has timed a run.
Player C is the 'third man' — they were not involved in the initial pass but exploit the space it creates.
Players rotate: A goes to B, B goes to C, C collects the ball and goes to A.
Run the pattern on both sides of the pitch.
coachingPoints: The third man run must be timed — start moving as the first pass is played, not before.
Player B's set must be accurate — angled to allow a first-time through ball.
Player A must have the vision to see the third man run developing.
Quality of the through ball is critical — weight it into the space, not to feet.
variations: Add a defender to track Player C's run.
Finish with a cross or shot on goal after receiving the through ball.
Combine two patterns simultaneously on both sides.

title: One-Touch Shooting Circle
instructions: Set up a semicircle of cones around the penalty area at 20 yards from goal.
Place a ball at each cone. Players line up behind one cone.
First player runs to the first cone, shoots first-time, then sprints to the next cone.
Shoot at every cone around the semicircle — all first-time.
Goalkeeper stays in goal for continuous action.
After completing the arc, jog back and next player goes. 3 rounds each.
coachingPoints: Set your body early — don't arrive at the ball off-balance.
Pick your target before you reach the ball.
Hit the target — accuracy beats power at this range.
Stay composed even when fatigued — game situations demand it.
variations: A server plays each ball in instead of having them placed.
Alternate between left foot and right foot at each station.
Add a time limit to complete the arc.

title: Stepovers & Scissors Drill
instructions: Set up 4 cones in a straight line, 6 yards apart. Place a gate (2 cones, 2 yards wide) next to each.
Dribble toward the first gate. Perform a single stepover and exit through the gate.
At the second gate, perform a double stepover (scissors) and exit.
At the third gate, perform a reverse stepover and exit.
At the fourth gate, combine any two moves and accelerate through.
Jog back and repeat. Complete 8 runs.
coachingPoints: Circle the ball fully with the stepover — don't just dangle your foot.
Drop the shoulder in the direction of the fake to sell it.
Exit with the outside of the opposite foot — push the ball away at pace.
Speed up the stepovers as you become comfortable.
variations: Add a passive defender standing at each gate.
Race a partner through parallel courses.
Finish with a shot on goal after the final gate.

title: Box-to-Box Intervals
instructions: Use the full pitch — start on one penalty box line.
Sprint to the halfway line, perform 5 ball taps, sprint to the opposite penalty box.
At the far box, perform 10 quick feet on the ball, then sprint back to halfway.
At halfway, do 5 push-ups, then sprint back to the start.
That is one rep. Rest 45 seconds between reps.
Complete 6 reps total.
coachingPoints: Maintain sprint quality — don't jog the second half of each sprint.
Ball work at the stations must be fast and purposeful, not sloppy.
Breathe rhythmically during push-ups to recover while working.
This drill simulates the demands of a box-to-box midfielder — replicate match intensity.
variations: Replace push-ups with burpees for extra intensity.
Add a pass-and-receive station at halfway with a partner.
Extend to full pitch length for higher fitness demands.

title: Long Ball Switching Play
instructions: Set up two wide zones (10x10 yards) on opposite sides of the pitch, 40 yards apart.
Place 3 players in each wide zone. One ball starts in the left zone.
Players in the left zone combine with quick passes (3 minimum).
After the combination, one player plays a long diagonal switch to the right zone.
Right zone players control, combine, and switch back to the left zone.
Rotate one player from each zone every 3 minutes.
coachingPoints: Long pass technique: lock ankle, lean slightly back, strike through the bottom half of the ball.
Receiving the long ball: get in line, cushion with the chest or thigh, set it for the next pass.
Quick combination before the switch creates rhythm — don't rush the long ball.
Communicate with the far zone — call for the ball, signal where you want it.
variations: Add a central defender who tries to intercept the long switch.
One-touch combinations before the switch.
Require a specific type of long pass: driven, lofted, or chipped.

title: Double Cut & Explode
instructions: Set up pairs of cones as gates (2 yards wide), staggered left and right, 5 yards apart.
Dribble toward the first gate. Perform a cut (inside of the foot) to change direction through the gate.
Immediately perform a second cut with the other foot to redirect toward the next gate.
The 'double cut' simulates changing direction twice to beat a defender.
Accelerate between gates. Complete 6 full runs through all gates.
Focus on close control and quick feet.
coachingPoints: Plant the non-cutting foot firmly and cut with the inside of the other foot.
The second cut must be immediate — no pause between the two cuts.
Stay low with bent knees to change direction quickly.
Accelerate explosively after the double cut — that's where you gain the advantage.
variations: Use outside-of-the-foot cuts instead of inside.
Alternate between inside and outside cuts.
Add a race element with a partner on a parallel course.

title: Near Post / Far Post Finishing
instructions: Goalkeeper in goal. Two servers stand wide, one on each side, with a supply of balls.
Striker starts centrally at the edge of the box.
Server 1 plays a low ball across the face of goal — striker attacks the near post to finish.
Striker immediately recovers to center. Server 2 plays a ball to the far post — striker finishes.
That is one rep. Complete 8 reps, then rotate the striker.
Emphasis on quick transitions between near and far post.
coachingPoints: Near post: get across the defender, attack the ball with a side-foot redirect.
Far post: arrive late, keep the ball low, sweep it into the net.
Recovery between shots must be game-speed — don't walk back to center.
Read the flight of the ball early and adjust your run accordingly.
variations: Add a defender who tries to block the striker's run.
Servers vary height — low, bouncing, or in the air.
Two strikers competing for the same ball.

title: Defensive Block 4-4-2 Shape
instructions: Set up a half-pitch with a full-size goal. 8 defenders form a 4-4-2 block.
6 attackers (plus a goalkeeper) try to break through and score.
Defenders must maintain compact shape — no more than 25 yards between the front and back line.
When the ball goes wide, the entire block shifts. When it's central, the block narrows.
Defenders win by forcing a turnover and clearing the ball past the halfway line.
Play 5-minute rounds, then rotate attackers and defenders.
coachingPoints: Move as a block — if one line shifts, the other must follow.
Distances matter: 10-12 yards between each line, 5-8 yards between players.
Near-side players press, far-side players tuck in.
Be patient — don't break shape to chase the ball, let the block do the work.
variations: Switch to a 4-5-1 or 5-3-2 shape.
Allow defenders to counter-attack through mini goals on the halfway line.
Add a time limit — if attackers don't score in 90 seconds, defenders win.

title: Ladder & Footwork Circuit
instructions: Lay out an agility ladder (or mark rungs with cones 18 inches apart).
Station 1: Two feet in each rung — quick high knees through the ladder.
Station 2: Lateral shuffle — two feet in each rung moving sideways.
Station 3: In-in-out-out (Icky Shuffle) — one foot in, other in, first out, second out.
Station 4: Single-leg hop through each rung.
Complete each station twice. Rest 20 seconds between stations.
coachingPoints: Stay on the balls of your feet — no heel strikes.
Pump the arms to drive foot speed.
Accuracy before speed — don't trip on the rungs.
Keep the core engaged and torso upright.
variations: Add a ball — dribble after exiting the ladder.
Time each station and track improvement over weeks.
Combine two patterns in one run for advanced footwork.
